Declan Rice romped through the middle at one point and the winning goal owed much to Reece James losing track of Martin Ødegaard as Arsenal’s captain strode throughto fire past Emiliano Martínez.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead moreIt was expected to be a key battleground, and the way Arsenal went 2-1 up was felt keenly by Chelsea given their difficulties on deadline day,when Enzo Fernández got his £125m move to Manchester Cityand no one was signed to replace the Argentinian. However, it is worth remembering Chelsea were short not only of Fernández’s offensive skills as they fell to their first defeat under Alonso. It was also significant that Moisés Caicedo was out again, an unspecified issue proving a nuisance, and it is a concern that Alonso lacks a suitable stand‑in for the Ecuador international whose ability to cover ground, snap into challenges and shield his defence would have come in handy against a midfield as powerful as Arsenal’s.There is much to like about Alonso’s vision.Chelseaare not obsessed with possession and are speeding forward on the counterattack. Yet while they look menacing with every attack there is a cost to the chaos. Alonso has found balance elusive. Chelsea have conceded seven goals in three games, are without a clean sheet in the league since January and need the oomph provided by Caicedo if they are to make this full-throttle style work.Caicedo, such an important presence since joining for £115m in 2023, is yet to start this season. He missedthe 3-2 win against Fulhamand was replaced 14 minutes after coming on duringthe 4-3 victory against Brighton. Alonso is erring on the side of caution. He stressed there was no long-term problem after the Arsenal game and admitted Caicedo was rushed back against Brighton. “I don’t want to make the same mistake again,” Alonso said, keeping the wider picture in mind. It is a long season, even with no European football, and the physical demands of the league means there is no point Caicedo playing through pain when doing so would surely cause more problems down the line.View image in fullscreenRomeo Lavia and Cole Palmer (right) of Chelsea try to dispossess Myles Lewis-Skelly of Arsenal.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAs it stands, though, Chelsea are too open and cannot strengthen until January. Compromises are necessary but the jury is out on some fixes.Alonso is a believer in James, whose shift from right‑back to central midfielder started under Enzo Maresca, but the captain is learning the role and his lack of feel for the position was exposed by Ødegaard.Arsenal found the gaps. Roméo Lavia started alongside James but is yet to complete 90 minutes since joining Chelsea three years ago. The Belgian has struggled with injuries and ran out of steam againstArsenalafter an hour, at which point Alonso looked to his bench and replaced Lavia with Malo Gusto, leaving his expensively assembled side to play out the closing stages with two repurposed right-backs in the middle.This was never the plan. Chelsea looked at replacements for Fernández. They wanted Alex Scott but Bournemouth would not sell. Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton has admirers, there was interest in Roma’s Manu Koné, whilea move for Monaco’s Lamine Camara,which collapsed as the summer window closed, left Chelsea fuming.In January Chelsea will hope to find a player more suited to Alonso’s system than Fernández, who is not the most mobile. They are not missing him in an attacking sense. Chelsea are scoring and the bigger headache is what to do out of possession. They do not have another player with Caicedo’s skillset.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDário Essugo was billed as Caicedo’s deputy when he joined last year but does not have Alonso’s trust and has been loaned to Strasbourg. Jordan Henderson is recovering from a broken wrist and is 36, and sending on Gusto over Valentín Barco was an early pointer. Barco, signed from Strasbourg this summer, is promising but the 22-year-old is inexperienced and, in any case, is more passer than destroyer.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Arsenal started with Rice, Ødegaard and Myles Lewis‑Skelly in midfield. They kept the £75m Bruno Guimarães in reserve and brought on two Spanish World Cup winners in Mikel Merino and Martín Zubimendi, another player wanted by Chelsea.The gulf in midfield resources told and it was the absence of Caicedo that mattered most for Chelsea. Perhaps Alonso could have adjusted and fallen back. If Chelsea continue to look so vulnerable at the back in the big games the tactics will be called naive. Yet Alonso will trust that sticking to his ideals will be rewarded in the long run. This is the start of a process. He is introducing a new system and accepts it comes with risks. The problem is that he does not have a midfielder to put out fires if Caicedo is out.Explore more on these topicsChelseaXabi AlonsoArsenalfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Joey Barton to remain in custody until trial after bail application turned down | Joey Barton | The Guardian
description: The former footballer stands accused of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, with his trial now pushed back to March next year
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The former footballer stands accused of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, with his trial now pushed back to March next year
Content: Joey Barton has had a renewed bail application refused.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenJoey Barton has had a renewed bail application refused.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAJoey BartonJoey Barton to remain in custody until trial after bail application turned downFormer footballer accused of attack outside golf clubHis trial has been pushed back to March next yearPress AssociationMon 7 Sep 2026 12.36 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 13.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe former footballerJoey Bartonwill remain in custody until his trial next year after a bail application was refused.The 44-year-old had been due to stand trial at Liverpool crown court last weekaccused of causing grievous bodily harm with intentto Kevin Lynch, 51, at Fairway, Huyton, on 8 March. But on Wednesday the case was adjourned and put back to March next year.Barton, wearing a grey zip-up fleece, appeared over video link from HMP Liverpool at a hearing on Monday, when the judge David Potter refused a renewed bail application. Barton nodded as the judge remanded him in custody in advance of a pre-trial hearing on 11 December.His trial will take place exactly a year after the alleged assault, meaning the defendant, who was arrested shortly after the incident, will have spent 12 months on remand.Barton is accused of carrying out the attack on Lynch after they had been drinking together at Huyton and Prescot golf club. Lynch, a former non-league football manager and founder of the special education school NexGen Academy, was said to have sustained serious injuries to an eye.Barton, the former Manchester City and QPR midfielder, of Widnes, Cheshire, won one England cap and also played for Newcastle, Rangers, Burnley and Marseille. After stopping playing he moved into coaching and had managerial spells at Fleetwood and Bristol Rovers.Explore more on these topicsJoey BartonnewsShareReuse this content

title: WSL talking points: Palace result in doubt after substitution nightmare, Arsenal signings shine | Women's football | The Guardian
description: Promoted side’s thrilling win may be overturned after they used four substitutions windows while Georgia Stanway show the way for Gunners
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Promoted side’s thrilling win may be overturned after they used four substitutions windows while Georgia Stanway show the way for Gunners
Content: Manchester City’s Lauren Hemp, Palace’s Lexi Lloyd-Smith and Arsenal debutant Lisa Baum.Composite: Shutterstock, GettyView image in fullscreenManchester City’s Lauren Hemp, Palace’s Lexi Lloyd-Smith and Arsenal debutant Lisa Baum.Composite: Shutterstock, GettyWomen's footballWSL talking points: Palace result in doubt after substitution nightmare, Arsenal signings shinePromoted side’s thrilling win may be overturned after they used four substitutions windows while Georgia Stanway show the way for GunnersSuzanne Wrack,Tom Garry,Sophie DowneyandRéshma RaoMon 7 Sep 2026 07.20 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 10.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThreat of punishment ruins Palace’s big dayKirsty Howat’s 60-second cameo deep into injury time could ruin what was a memorable day for Crystal Palace on their return to the top flight. An impressive 1-0 victory over Everton was celebrated emphatically by Jo Potter and her players but that joy would have been replaced by concern and frustration not long after. On Sunday evening WSL Football revealed that there had been a breach of the rules – the Eagles used four different substitute windows rather than the regulated three – which had not been picked up by either the coaching staff or the match officials. An investigation has now been launched with punishment to be decided (there is a potential for the result to be overturned). The needless error has put a dampener on what should have been a positive afternoon thanks to England Under-23s forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s winner on her WSL debut.Sophie DowneyChelsea must sharpen their clawsIt was not the first time Chelsea have struggled to kill off games under Sonia Bompastor and, on the basis ofSaturday’s 1-1 draw with Aston Villaafter an almost excessively dominant performance, it seems the issues of last season have not been put to bed. “I think in a few games we had last season we were in the same scenarios,” said Bompastor. “So, yeah, if you analyse the performance today and the statistics of the game you can say that it’s crazy we couldn’t win the game.” It felt all too familiar, with last season’s 1-0 defeat to Everton in December, which ended a 585-day unbeaten run in the WSL, particularly springing to mind. Then, Chelsea accrued 79% possession, had 30 shots and hit the woodwork three times but came away with a loss. The fear for Chelsea fans will be that, in the 10 months since that defeat, the issues that were becoming increasingly evident have not been resolved.Suzanne WrackMatch report:Chelsea 1-1 Aston VillaView image in fullscreenSjoeke Nüsken (left) shields the ball in Chelsea’s game against Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Jermaine Addo-Yeboah/SPP/ShutterstockSignings shine on competitive debut for ArsenalMuch has been made of Arsenal’s recruitment over the summer with many believing that Renée Slegers now has a team primed to challenge for the title. Four of their new signings started in the 1-0 win over Brighton, with two standing out. Recognition of Lisa Baum’s potential came to the fore with a series of impressive showings in pre-season. The 19-year-old caught the eye on her WSL debut on Sunday not just for her well-taken goal but for her direct, positive style of play. Meanwhile, Georgia Stanway showed exactly why Slegers was so keen to bring her in. The England international has added balance to the midfield, allowing Mariona Caldentey to operate more creatively. Stanway controlled the middle of the park, ranking first for touches – at 131, she had 25 more than anyone else – joint top for accurate passes (86%), first for passes into the final third (23) and second for chances created (2).SDRole model Hemp brings up double century“Just give her the ball and then something happens!” Andrée Jeglertz said of Lauren Hemp after her 200th appearance for Manchester City. The England winger was on typically strong form during the 3-1 victory over Birmingham City and became only the fourth Manchester City player to reach that landmark of appearances. Jeglertz was full of praise for the 26-year-old and continued: “One thing that is fascinating with Lauren is, if you come and watch one of our training sessions, she has the same joy for playing football. It’s also shown in the games. Our job is to put her in situations where she can show how good she is. [She] shows young players what it’s about. They need to love to go to work and love to go to the football field. It’s not just a job. It’s also an identity.”Tom GarryMaestre masters the melting potMany believe the biggest challenges faced by theLondon City Lionessesmanager, Eder Maestre, is integrating a squad that has experienced a high turnover of players and balancing the demands of an expectant cast of superstars. There have been eight arrivals this summer and seven players have departed. Teams that have experienced a high turnover of players after a strong WSL season have previously struggled. On Friday night, however, Maestre’s team showed signs they could buck that trend with a 2-1 win over Manchester United. It wasn’t always the prettiest of performances but fledgling connections were forming in Bromley, with the individual quality of players helping to cut across any lack of cohesion. Gelling players is not easy though. “I think it’s one of the most challenging situations for any coach,” said Maestre. “We have talented players, but we have a clash of cultures. I’m trying to align everybody in the same place, trying to create something big where everybody can feel represented … I’m very happy with the performance.”SWMatch report:London City Lionesses 2-1 Manchester Unitedskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenDaniëlle Van De Donk (centre) peels away after scoring London City Lionesses’ winner against Manchester United.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAre Charlton strong enough to stay up?It was a worrying start to the season for Charlton Athletic fans, as the newly promoted side were convincingly beaten on home turf by the club that finished second from bottom in the WSL last season. Not only that, Charlton failed to register a shot on target during Liverpool’s 4-0 victory and the hosts could only manage two efforts off target, as Gareth Taylor’s visitors’ enjoyed 76% of the possession. It had been a much closer-fought affair when the two sides met on the same ground on April in the Women’s FA Cup quarter-finals, when Liverpool eventually squeezed through after extra-time, but the Merseyside club appear to have strengthened significantly over the summer whereas Charlton clearly have significant work to do.TGHanson makes instant impact for Spurs with debut doubleKirsty Hanson wasted no time making her mark at Tottenham, scoring twice on her debut to secure a 3-1 victory over West Ham after joining from Aston Villa this summer. The forward opened her account with a first-time finish after an assist from Signe Gaupset and then produced a superb left-footed strike into the top corner. Hanson was the third-highest scorer in the WSL last season, behind Bunny Shaw and Alessia Russo, with 12 goals in 22 matches. She was one of several key transfers made during the window with the club believing she will add a new dimension to their attack. Speaking to Spurs Women social media about her performance, the manager, Martin Ho, said: “The movement for her first one was outstanding, and the second was a wonderful strike. When she’s in those positions with that quality and control, she’s really hard to play against. There’s lots more to come from Kirsty.”Réshma RaoSuzanne Wrack answered your questions about the WSL as part the Guardian’s new Q&A seriesConversationsExplore more on these topicsWomen's footballCrystal Palace WomenEverton WomenChelsea WomenAston Villa WomenArsenal WomenBrighton & Hove Albion WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Monaco kept their best players and are top of Ligue 1 – but at what cost? | Ligue 1 | The Guardian
description: You might think Monaco have plenty to cheer about, especially after their 2-1 win at PSG, but it’s complicated
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: You might think Monaco have plenty to cheer about, especially after their 2-1 win at PSG, but it’s complicated
Content: Monaco players celebrate after their 2-1 win against PSG at the Parc des Princes.Photograph: Yoan Valat/EPAView image in fullscreenMonaco players celebrate after their 2-1 win against PSG at the Parc des Princes.Photograph: Yoan Valat/EPAGuardian Sport NetworkLigue 1Monaco kept their best players and are top of Ligue 1 – but at what cost?You might think Monaco have plenty to cheer about, especially after their 2-1 win at PSG, but it’s complicatedByGet French Football NewsLuke EntwistleMon 7 Sep 2026 10.59 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 11.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhen a manager says that “no player is more important than the club”, it is usually because said player is agitating for a move. Filipe Luís was referring to Folarin Balogun, who did quite the opposite on transfer deadline day,opting to stay at Monacorather than joining Everton, despite an agreement between the clubs.You’d think that retaining your top scorer from last season would be reason for celebration, but the fact it is not once again exposes the French football paradox. Like plenty of other clubs inLigue 1, Monaco are torn between sporting and financial prerogatives. They ended up prioritising the former on transfer deadline day, albeit unwillingly, and even in a week when they beat PSG at the Parc des Princes to retain their 100% record, it is bittersweet.Monaco went into deadline day prepared to make a sacrifice. Balogun was their top scorer last season and had shone at the World Cup for USA, but his exit had been planned. Matthis Abline had arrived from Nantes at the start of the window to take his place and everything was going “as planned” in the words of the club’s CEO, Thiago Scuro.It wasn’t so simple though. In the midst of Balogun’s on-again-off-again move to Everton, Monaco agreed and then reneged on a deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea. No manager would want to lose the midfielder, but Monaco had been forced to accept Chelsea’s offer, having made promises to French football’s financial watchdog, the DNCG, to reduce the wage bill and raise considerable funds in player sales. However, by the time a deal was struck with Chelsea, the French transfer window had closed and Camara’s replacement, Érik Lira, was no longer an option, especially given that the non-EU spot, occupied by Balogun, had not been vacated as planned.Ultimately, neither Camara nor Balogun left. Good news, you might think. If it was, you couldn’t necessarily tell in Scuro’s hastily convened press conference on Wednesday, when the club’s CEO rallied against the idea that Monaco were “the bad guys in the room” following the series of unfortunate events the night before. “Unfortunately, we have to face this situation and find solutions in different ways,” added Scuro. It remains to be seen what the solutions are.Luís, meanwhile, bemoaned an “imbalanced” squad: too many centre-forwards, a lack of midfield cover, and no recognised right-winger after Maghnes Akliouche’s move to PSG. The squad may lack balance and the club did not bring in the money they need, but the reason for their despondency is also the reason they can now harbour greater ambitions for the season. Balogun was Monaco’s best player last season; Camara has been their best player so far this season. If Camara was affected by the Chelsea saga, it did not show on Friday night. He was excellent in the second half as Monaco came from behind to beat PSG, with goals from Nazinho and Stanis Idumbo securing the 2-1 win.Luís – who played for Atlético Madrid, Chelsea and Flamengo, as well as Brazil – says a big move will come for Camara. “If he maintains his level, it won’t just be one club – all the big clubs will come for him,” said the manager, adding that the 22-year-old is “unbelievable”, “elite”, and that “there aren’t a lot of players like him in football”. Scuro hinted that there would be “even better options and offers” in the future for the Senegal international. An eventual departure is expected, but Monaco should at least try to live in the present – as much as the spectre of financial obligations looms.The manager has plenty of talent at his disposal and Balogun, who has missed the first few games of the season, is set to return soon. Without their top scorer from last season, Monaco have won their first five fixtures of the campaign in all competitions, scoring 12 goals in the process. The club’s decision to sack Sébastien Pocognoli in the summer looked harsh, but no one could complain about the start Luís has made. Not even the legendary Arsène Wenger enjoyed a better start at Monaco than the Brazilian.View image in fullscreenFilipe Luís has enjoyed an excellent start at Monaco.Photograph: Loic Baratoux/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockLuís was full of praise for Luis Enrique, naming him as one of the top five managers in history. And the respect is mutual. “He is a manager I like a lot,” said the PSG boss. “I was happy when I found out that he was coming to France, then I told myself that I maybe shouldn’t be.” The pair faced each other in the Intercontinental Cup last year, when Flamengo – who won the Copa Libertadores under Luís – held PSG to a 1-1 draw before the French side won a penalty shootout.Monaco are the only team to have won their first three Ligue 1 games this season. They have kept their best players, bar Akliouche, and they have a highly rated manager who is enhancing his reputation every week. There is plenty to cheer about, at least on the face of things, but the reasons for optimism are also the reasons for concern; such is the paradox that afflicts Monaco.Quick GuideLigue 1 resultsShowTroyes 2-6 StrasbourgAngers 1-2 RennesMarseille 2-3 Paris FCLens 0-1 LorientLe Havre 1-2 BrestNice 1-1 Le MansLyon 3-1 AuxerrePSG 1-2 MonacoToulouse 0-1 LilleWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Talking points“Ça se prolonge,” read the front page ofL’Équipeon Saturday. “It’s extended” was not only a reference to Luis Enrique, Fabián Ruiz, João Neves, Willian Pacho, Senny Mayulu and Lucas Beraldo extending their contracts, but also to PSG’s winless run in Ligue 1 this season. The last time PSG began a campaign without a win in their first three was in 2012. PSG won the league that season and there isn’t too much concern this time around. “In my first two seasons, we had a habit of not winning games at the start of the season, and at the end we won everything,” said Neves post-match. Luis Enrique said he was willing to bet that PSG would finish the season as champions. Even if the European champions are in the bottom half of the table, seven points off leaders Monaco, few would bet against them securing their sixth consecutive Ligue 1 title come May.Bruno Génésio did not want to catastrophise after Marseille’s 2-0 defeat to Monaco last weekend but he admitted there was “cause for concern” after he watched his team lose 3-2 at home to Paris FC on Sunday. Lassine Sinayoko scored a hat-trick for the visitors, with his first goal coming after just 23 seconds. There is a glaring lack of quality and depth in thisMarseilleside. Génésio said his players made “too many big errors” but he cannot replace many of them. On the bench he only had raw, untested prospects and players who have returned from loan spells after failing to secure contracts elsewhere. Amine Harit, who is back in the team after a loan in Turkey, says he and his teammates are “giving 100%”. That hasn’t always been the case at Marseille. title: Pakistan launch player conduct investigation during dysfunctional England tour | Pakistan cricket team | The Guardian
description: Pakistan have launched an investigation into ‘discipline and conduct’ during their highly dysfunctional tour of England, with two players understood to have had their mobile phones confiscated as part of the inquiry
Author: Ali Martin
Headline: Pakistan have launched an investigation into ‘discipline and conduct’ during their highly dysfunctional tour of England, with two players understood to have had their mobile phones confiscated as part of the inquiry
Content: King Charles poses with members of the Pakistan cricket team during an audience at Clarence House earlier in September.Photograph: Stefan Rousseau/ReutersView image in fullscreenKing Charles poses with members of the Pakistan cricket team during an audience at Clarence House earlier in September.Photograph: Stefan Rousseau/ReutersPakistan cricket teamPakistan launch player conduct investigation during dysfunctional England tourMobile phones of players confiscated as part of inquiryNine fined during Pakistan’s recent tour of CaribbeanAli MartinMon 7 Sep 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 11.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePakistan have launched an investigation into “discipline and conduct” during their highly dysfunctional tour of England, with two players understood to have had their mobile phones confiscated as part of the probe.A spokesperson for the PakistanCricketBoard confirmed on Monday that an investigation is currently under way and while no individuals have been named, it follows the removal of seven players from their original touring party last week in response to going 2-0 down with one Test still to play.Azhar Ali: ‘Pakistan cricket cannot change in the space of a year’Read moreThe Guardian understands that, as part of this, two players had data from their mobile phones captured by PCB security officials. This is said to have occurred during the aftermath of the team’s 194-run defeat in the second Test at Lord’s.Amir Mir, the PCB head of communications,wrote on X: “The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.“The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.”The precise nature of the investigation – ie any potential wrongdoing or otherwise – is not yet clear, nor has a timeline been announced.So far only Imam-ul-Haq has drawn the public ire of the PCB – and a large section of supporters – after the opener did not bat in either innings of the Lord’s defeat due to a low-grade calf injury suffered on day one.Speaking in an interview with Geo News last week, Aaqib Javed, Pakistan’s director of high performance, said: “The Imam injury is a big question mark, and a deep disappointment.“Players in the past used to get injuries, but they used to put on casts and still tried [to play]. We’ll take action against this. How is it possible that a pulled muscle ruled you out of batting in both innings? He should have tried and fought.“He’ll have to face an inquiry; I can’t say he faked it, but a muscle pull like that cannot stop you from batting altogether.”Imam has since been released from the squad, along with Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad and the unused Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Zafar. Sarfraz Ahmed was also stood down as head coach, with New Zealander Mike Hesson moved across from his role with the white-ball team.Speaking after training at Edgbaston on Monday, Pakistan’s newly arrived bowling coach, Ashley Noffke, said: “I don’t know too much.“I sit outside that decision-making model above us as coaches. We try to keep the players focused on what they need to worry about.“I guess that’s one thing I’ve learned about being in Pakistan and coaching for a period of time – nearly 15 months with the white-ball team – there’s always something going on in the background, whether or not it’s in or out of our control – and most of the time it’s out of the players’ control.”As well as this ongoing investigation, the upheaval has also triggered news of nine players being fined during Pakistan’s recent tour of the Caribbean.The Guardian understands this was considered a relatively minor issue. The players were supposed to stay within the Player and Match Officials Areas (PMOA) during their warm-up match in Trinidad, only for a group to break away to watch the Fifa World Cup final in a part of the ground not covered by the restrictions.Explore more on these topicsPakistan cricket teamEngland v Pakistan 2026England cricket teamCricketnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Relief’ of Premier League title has given Arsenal confidence, says David Raya  | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: David Raya says Arsenal are playing with greater confidence after the ‘relief’ of winning the Premier League
Author: David Hytner
Headline: David Raya says Arsenal are playing with greater confidence after the ‘relief’ of winning the Premier League
Content: Arsenal's David Raya praised the side’s reaction after conceding early against Chelsea.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersView image in fullscreenArsenal's David Raya praised the side’s reaction after conceding early against Chelsea.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersArsenal‘Relief’ of Premier League title has given Arsenal confidence, says David RayaKeeper says Gunners ‘can beat anybody in this league’Arteta’s side have started title defence with three winsDavid HytnerMon 7 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 17.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDavid Raya says Arsenal are playing with greater confidence after the “relief” of winning the Premier League. The champions continued their perfect start to the defence of their crown with the2-1 home win against Chelseaon Sunday, making it nine points out of nine.It was a powerhouse performance coloured by a freedom of expression, which stood in contrast to the nerviness of the final months of last season when the team laboured under a weight of pressure and expectation beforethey beat Manchester City to the title. That was Arsenal’s first triumph since 2004 and followed three consecutive runners-up finishes.Wild opening salvo against Chelsea hints at exciting times for Arsenal fans | Barney RonayRead moreThe shackles were off against Chelsea, just as they have been for much of the season, beginning with the3-0 win against City in the Community Shield. Kai Havertz and Martin Ødegaard scored the goals against Chelsea and provided most of the creative flourishes. But it was the ferocity of the collective intensity, the sheer physicality, that took the breath. Raya pulled off a stunning late save to deny the Chelsea substitute Estêvão. Arsenal did not deserve to drop points. It was an ominous statement of intent.“Winning the league after that many years and after those years that you are so close … it gives you that relief and it gives you that extra confidence,” Raya said. “Coming from the three games this season, especially the Community Shield, winning against City, the way we played against them – that gives you extra motivation and extra confidence to play the way we want to play …“Hopefully we can keep playing this way because we know how good we are. We know we can beat anybody in this league. Let’s just focus on the moment and be in the present.”The most eye-catching aspect of the display was howArsenalreacted to going behind after 77 seconds to a Morgan Rogers volley. They attacked in waves and created a remarkable number of openings before Havertz equalised in the 25th minute. The belief could also be felt in the stands where there was no panic, only bellowed encouragement.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“There’s things to improve on that goal [by Rogers],” Raya said. “We had to defend a little bit better, especially right at the start of the game. It was disappointing to concede that goal. But the main thing is the reaction that we had after it and the way we played. The way we dominated, the way we attacked, we defended.“We know how good Chelsea are, especially in transitions, and the way the play is dragged back to defend. So it was a really important win.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Kevin Pietersen gets surprise call-up as mentor for England cricket team | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: Kevin Pietersen has been appointed as a ‘specialist mentor’ to England’s white-ball teams during the run-up to the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup in late 2027
Author: Ali Martin
Headline: Kevin Pietersen has been appointed as a ‘specialist mentor’ to England’s white-ball teams during the run-up to the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup in late 2027
Content: Kevin Pietersen has been appointed as a ‘specialist mentor’ to England’s white-ball teams.Photograph: Mihir Singh/ReutersView image in fullscreenKevin Pietersen has been appointed as a ‘specialist mentor’ to England’s white-ball teams.Photograph: Mihir Singh/ReutersEngland cricket teamKevin Pietersen gets surprise call-up as mentor for England cricket teamFirst time former captain involved since 2014 sackingJoins McCullum’s backroom staff for the next yearAli MartinMon 7 Sep 2026 06.08 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKevin Pietersen will return to the England fold 12 years on from his acrimonious sacking as a player after being appointed as a “specialist mentor” to the men’s white-ball teams until the end of the 50-over Cricket World Cup next year.Announced on Monday morning, this consultancy deal marks the first time Pietersen will have worked with the senior England side since his central contract was ripped up in the wake of the 2013-14 Ashes ­whitewash in Australia.Carse left out in cold again and told to ‘work through issues’ after Derby bar incidentRead morePietersen, 46, has worked as a TV commentator and an online content creator since he stopped playing in 2018 and will join Brendon McCullum’s white-ball coaching staff for the home fixtures against Sri Lanka this month. The deal runs until the end of the World Cup in late 2027, albeit with Pietersen due to miss a one-day international tri-series in Pakistan that takes place this October.Pietersen said: “I am immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa. Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment.“We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad, and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential. To be a part of Brendon’s thinktank over the next 12 months is a fantastic opportunity, and I cannot wait to get started.”Drafting in such a strong – and at times divisive – character represents a bold move by McCullum. Pietersen has also criticised the New Zealander in recent times, including the white-ball team’s approach to training during a tour of India last year and the Test side’s preparations before last winter’s Ashes series.Nevertheless, Pietersen’s pedigree as an all-format international is not in question, nor his own dedication to training and preparation in his playing days. Indeed a number of current players have cited Pietersen as an influence growing up, while Harry Brook, the white-ball captain, has drawn comparisons as a batter.The England statement also noted Pietersen’s knowledge of South Africa, hosts for the 2027 World Cup along with Namibia and Zimbabwe. He joins a setup that includes the assistant coaches Marcus Trescothick and Jeetan Patel, with Sarah Taylor in charge of fielding/wicketkeeping and Tim Southee overseeing the bowlers.McCullum,who was sacked as Test head coachin July, said: “I’ve got immense respect for KP and what he’s achieved in the game. He’s had an amazing impact on English cricket, so for someone with his experience, knowledge and stature to want to play a role with this team is a fantastic result.“ I’m particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him. KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players.“We’ve always respected each other and had a strong appreciation for what the other brings to the game, so I’m really looking forward to ­working together.”Pietersen’s deal was announced as England’s Test players tuned up for the third Test against Pakistan, which gets under way at Edgbaston on Wednesday. Joe Root’s side have the chance to secure a 3-0 clean sweep, with the tourists having dropped seven players from their original squad in response to last week’s defeat at Lord’s.Despite a summer of quickfire Test matches where the ball has dominated, Jofra Archer is wary of an Edgbaston pitch on which last year’s defeat to India went the distance, with Shubman Gill scoring 430 runs across two innings. Archer said: “It’s early days [for this attack] but we’ve been going all right so far. This pitch usually goes five days, so we’ll see how we go if we have the opportunity to be out there a bit longer than the past two games. But, regardless, everyone is very relentless.”Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamKevin PietersenBrendon McCullumCricketnewsShareReuse this content

title: Warning over future of Olympic Games if Brisbane 2032 program is not modernised | Brisbane Olympic Games 2032 | The Guardian
description: Australia’s most senior sport executive, Kieren Perkins, has called on the IOC to update the sporting program for Brisbane 2032
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: Australia’s most senior sport executive, Kieren Perkins, has called on the IOC to update the sporting program for Brisbane 2032
Content: Gridiron, baseball, cricket, squash, softball and lacrosse have been included for LA 2028 and Kieren Perkins has called for more innovation at the 2032 Brisbane Games.Photograph: Mark Evans/Getty Images for the AOCView image in fullscreenGridiron, baseball, cricket, squash, softball and lacrosse have been included for LA 2028 and Kieren Perkins has called for more innovation at the 2032 Brisbane Games.Photograph: Mark Evans/Getty Images for the AOCBrisbane Olympic Games 2032Warning over future of Olympic Games if Brisbane 2032 program is not modernisedKieren Perkins expresses concern over some traditional sportsDoor is open to likes of cricket and netball for Games in AustraliaJack SnapeMon 7 Sep 2026 03.14 EDTLast modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 07.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFormer gold-medal winning swimmer and Australia’s most senior sport executive, Kieren Perkins, has called on the IOC to modernise the sporting program for Brisbane 2032, arguing that some current Olympic sports “have no modern relevance whatsoever”.The IOC has indicated it wishes to curb a long-term trend of a rise in the number of sports at the Games. Sydney 2000 featured 28 sports, while Los Angeles 2028 is set to feature 36, including many with more than one discipline – for example road and track cycling – that require multiple venues.Queensland reveals concept plans for Brisbane Olympic stadium precinct – but critics say they are ‘fantasy vision’Read morePerkins, who is chief executive of government agency the Australian Sports Commission, said he has concerns for the future of the Olympic movement if the Brisbane 2032 program is not updated. “If that program doesn’t look different, then yes, we should start to worry,” he said at the SportNXT conference in Melbourne.“But if the Olympic movement actually does grasp the challenge that they’ve got, and recognise that while there are some traditional sports that we love dearly, they have no modern relevance whatsoever and there’s others that absolutely have earned and need a more prominent position within the Olympic movement.“If that’s embraced, then I think we’ll be fine, but if we can’t find a way to navigate through that, then there are question marks about that sustainability.”Perkins declined to name individual sports without modern relevance, but his comments will make some sporting officials nervous. Sports such as modern pentathlon and equestrian have passionate communities of players and supporters and long histories in the Olympics, but they cannot compete with the profile of core sports such as athletics and swimming.The recent re-introduction of cricket, baseball and softball to the Games for Los Angeles 2028 also highlights the competition for places in the program. Cricket Australia chair Mike Baird has called for the Olympic final in 2032 to be the last game at the Gabba. A spokesperson for Cricket Australia said it was continuing to work with the ICC to “advance cricket’s cause for inclusion” in the Brisbane program.“Cricket’s inclusion in Los Angeles 2028 will be a landmark moment for the game and our national teams showcasing the sport to our enormous global audiences as well as new cricket markets,” they said.Lacrosse, a sport invented by North American First Nations people, was also re-introduced into the Olympics for 2028. Chief executive of Lacrosse Australia, Anna Carroll, said the sport has “strong modern relevance” and its inclusion into the LA program “will introduce the sport to new audiences, inspire the next generation of players and strengthen participation pathways across Australia”. She added her organisation is working with World Lacrosse “to demonstrate the sport’s value to the Olympic movement”.Netball has also been lobbying for inclusion in the 2032 program, especially given its popularity among women. As part of its lobbying effort, Netball Australia commissioned independent polling earlier this year which found two thirds of Australians want netball played at Brisbane 2032.Rowing Australia chief executive Sarah Cook said rowing is “woven” into the country’s Olympic story but it also “continues to evolve and innovate”, including with the addition of beach sprints rowing at LA. “The Olympic programme should continue to evolve, like all major events,” she said. “But rowing’s rich history, global reach and ability to produce compelling sporting moments is part of what makes the Games special. We plan to add to that legacy in Brisbane in 2032.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe IOC session in June developed a new methodology to determine the Olympic program, including focusing on individual disciplines rather than sports. The local organising committees can propose a maximum of four additional disciplines. Each discipline will be assessed in terms of its global appeal, cost and operational complexity and the how well its athletes are represented in the sport’s governance.This will be applied with flexibility to Brisbane 2032, given preparations are advanced, and the program is expected to be finalised by the IOC within the next year.“The Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games Organising Committee has had strong interest from a range of sports wanting to be involved in the Games in 2032,” a Brisbane 2032 spokesperson said.“We are focused on designing a sports program that reflects the values of the Olympic and Paralympic movements, is operationally viable, and supports Brisbane 2032’s commercial, sustainable and engagement and experience objectives.”Modern pentathlon has taken the radical step of dropping equestrian from its sub-disciplines and replacing it with obstacle course ahead of the 2028 Olympics. Breaking, the controversial addition to the Paris program, was not retained for Los Angeles.Explore more on these topicsBrisbane Olympic Games 2032Olympic GamesAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Wallabies’ Carter Gordon set for stint on sidelines after breaking leg in latest injury blow  | Australia rugby union team | The Guardian
description: The Wallabies are bracing to be without first-choice playmaker Carter Gordon for the Bledisloe Cup and a clash with world champions South Africa in the latest injury blow for the flyhalf
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Wallabies are bracing to be without first-choice playmaker Carter Gordon for the Bledisloe Cup and a clash with world champions South Africa in the latest injury blow for the flyhalf
Content: Carter Gordon is expected to miss two months of rugby after breaking a bone in his leg during the Test against Argentina.Photograph: Matt King/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCarter Gordon is expected to miss two months of rugby after breaking a bone in his leg during the Test against Argentina.Photograph: Matt King/Getty ImagesAustralia rugby union teamWallabies’ Carter Gordon set for stint on sidelines after breaking leg in latest injury blowFlyhalf sustains injury in weekend’s draw with ArgentinaExpected to miss Springboks Test and Bledisloe Cup seriesAustralian Associated PressMon 7 Sep 2026 02.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Wallabies are bracing to be without first-choice playmaker Carter Gordon for the Bledisloe Cup and a clash with world champions South Africa in the latest injury blow for the flyhalf.Gordon fell to the ground in agony after attacking the line late in the weekend’s28-28 draw with Argentinain Mendoza.Wallabies’ key weakness lets Argentina off the hook, but Les Kiss won’t ‘catastrophise it’ | Jack SnapeRead moreThe side doesn’t land back in Australia until Monday night but it is understood scans post-game revealed the 25-year-old had suffered a leg fracture that will keep him sidelined for two months.That injury would rule him out of the Wallabies’ Perth Test against the Springboks on 26 September, as well as next month’s two-Test Bledisloe Cup series. There is hope he would be fit in time to face England at Twickenham on 8 November.It’s the latest injury blow for the luckless playmaker, who suffered a serious back injury that derailed his NRL cameo and has battled various leg niggles since returning to rugby barely a year ago.View image in fullscreenGordon is tackled by Argentina's Faustino Sanchez Valarolo.Photograph: Gustavo Garello/APBen Donaldson started in that position against Los Pumas for the first time in two years, but Gordon had established himself as the first-choice playmaker under Kiss.Donaldson failed to put his stamp on the contest and will now face stiff opposition to retain the jersey, with fit-again Reds flyhalf Tom Lynagh likely to return from a long injury absence of his own in Super Rugby AU, on Saturday against the Western Force.Declan Meredith started in three Tests this year and was in the Argentinian tour squad, while Harry McLaughlin-Phillips could also mount a case in new Force colours in the pre-season competition.Test veterans James O’Connor (Force) and Bernard Foley (NSW Waratahs) will make Super Rugby Pacific returns next year and both harbour World Cup aspirations, but will not feature in Super Rugby AU.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAustralia’s forwards have impressed during a five-game unbeaten streak but Gordon’s injury, as well as the form of fullback Tom Wright and lack of impact from big-money centre Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, mean question marks remain ahead of Kiss’s biggest test yet.“We know we’ve got to be better than what we were, but we can see the growth,” said in-form halfback Ryan Lonergan, who finished the game acting as flyhalf because of Gordon’s injury.“If we get our game together on both sides of the ball ... tidy up our attack, we’ve got a chance of pushing them [the Springboks] a long way.“Joe [former coach Schmidt] gave us a great platform to play off and now, with the continuity in the team and little changes and tweaks Les has brought into our attack, the ceiling for our attack has lifted and we look like we have more points in us. Now it’s about converting it.”Explore more on these topicsAustralia rugby union teamRugby unionAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content
